page_title: What distinguishes the Top 1% of product managers from the Top 10%?

sources.entry: What distinguishes the Top 1% of product managers from the Top 10%? - *(Quora)*

summary.title: What distinguishes the Top 1% of product managers from the Top 10%?
summary.one_liner: Ian McAllister's Quora answer lists ten traits, such as thinking big, simplifying, prioritizing, and writing effective copy, that he says separate elite product managers from merely good ones.
keywords: what makes a great product manager
takeaways: Top 1% PMs excel at most of ten listed skills, while Top 10% PMs excel at only a few.
Good PMs think big, constrained by neither today's resources nor the current market.
Prioritize by balancing quick wins against platform work and offense (growth) against defense (debt, bugs, operations).
Forecast and measure benefit of projects, then feed learnings back into future prioritization.
The author suggests hiring a 10% PM who strives to improve over trying to find a 1% PM.
summary.summary: A Quora answer by Ian McAllister responding to the question of what separates the top 1% of product managers from the top 10%. He describes ten dimensions: think big, communicate, simplify, prioritize, forecast and measure, execute, understand technical trade-offs, understand good design, and write effective copy. Each is a short paragraph describing the behavior of a 1% PM. The page also includes reader comments, which are mostly praise or light commentary and add no substantive facts.
